acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Raptors family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Carrion Kite, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Shadow-Dive Initiate archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Lean long-winged kite with forked tail, small hooked beak, narrow chest, and ordinary mottled plumage.
Signature mechanic: Shadow Crossing: the Kite commits exactly when its tightening shadow touches the target's feet.
battlefieldDuty: Circle once and dive when its shadow crosses the target.
constructionDimensions: Streaming wet feathers retain layered vanes around a solid body while coherent droplets trace wingbeats and tail turns.
Pressurized water gathers along talons and leading edges, then drains visibly at landing or perch recovery.
counterplay: Step across the shadow and punish the Kite during its low recovery climb. Affinity signal: The loaded wing or talon channel empties after release and exposes the same grounded joint or perch window.
forbiddenTreatments: Spray that hides the silhouette, shadow, or landing route
identityInvariants: Every form retains an avian body with two wings, two taloned legs, hooked beak, feathered tail, and species-appropriate head rather than humanoid arms or torso.
Tier escalation uses wingspan, feather structure, facial disc, talon mass, scars, and flight behavior rather than worn equipment.
Shadow shape, tail fan, primary-feather angle, talon extension, perch choice, and landing route keep aerial attacks readable.
telegraph: The shadow tightens and the wings briefly stop beating.
